evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2 l.53-56: "every count, state, rank, layout position and diff it shows arrives computed ... Its data is the payload of `tp epic export` and of `tp export` (§16)"; §2 l.58-61 lists the export additions (revision, generated_at, layout, lint, milestone state, §5 slice fields, bound_at/imported_at) — no snapshot differences or per-epic history; §11 l.259-263: "between two chosen rounds, the difference of their snapshots ... Per epic, the drawer shows how its edges and whys changed"; §16 l.359-360: "the difference of its spec snapshot from the round before"; §13 l.314: "between two review rounds the diff of their snapshots"; §17 l.402: "tasks closed".
finding: Several views must show a diff or history that §2 requires to arrive computed, but neither payload the page receives carries it: §11's difference "between two chosen rounds" of a slice (an arbitrary pair, while §5/§2 add only per-round counts to the export's slices), §11's per-epic edge/why history in the drawer (not among §2's export additions), §13's diff "between two review rounds" (§16 carries only each round's difference from the round before), and §17's "tasks closed" (a push of `tp epic export` + `tp export --list` holds task counts, not tasks). One implementation adds GET endpoints or extra payload fields; another composes consecutive diffs or count deltas in the page, which §2 and the Non-goals forbid. The spec also never says which `tp export` files the page receives (one per file pushed, or fetched on opening the Spec tab).
suggestion: State what the server serves beyond the two exports: e.g. the export's slices carry every consecutive snapshot difference and per-epic history, and a pair difference is a read-only GET backed by the same code as `tp epic review --history --from --to`; or narrow §11/§13 to consecutive rounds. Say whether per-file `tp export` payloads are pushed for every file or fetched when the Spec tab opens.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2: "Its data is the payload of `tp epic export` and of `tp export` (§16), produced in-process by the same code." vs §11: "Per epic, the drawer shows how its edges and whys changed across the snapshots of the slices it appears in. All of it is derived in Go from the slices' state directories, and the same derivation is a command: `tp epic review <slice> --history`". §5 lists only "each recorded round's finding count, total and by role" for the export. skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:1762: on `tp epic export` "`--compact` is ignored".
finding: The page's graph history (per-slice snapshot differences between any two rounds, and per-epic edge/why changes across every slice) has no stated source other than §2's rule that the page's data is the `tp epic export` and `tp export` payloads. §5 puts only per-round finding counts into the export's `slices[]`, so one correct implementation adds every slice's round-by-round snapshot differences to `tp epic export` (whose `--compact` is ignored), and another serves them separately. The first makes every agent export call pay for history that no planning decision reads: an agent picking ready work, checking a gate or grading a slice never needs round-to-round snapshot diffs, and the one that does has `tp epic review --history`.
suggestion: Say the page reads graph history from §11's `--history` derivation on demand (per slice, per epic), and that `tp epic export` carries none of it beyond §5's per-round counts; narrow §2's data sentence to match.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2 l.48-49: "pushes it to the page over Server-Sent Events only when its `revision` changed"; §2 l.58: "`tp epic export` gains ... `revision` (a hash of the payload's inputs)"; §18 row 3: "a task closed with `tp done` reaches the page | a repo with one task file, two ticks"; §16 l.381: "unbound files have no place in the graph's contract"; skills/tp/SKILL.md l.797: `tp epic export` "Exit 0; 3 with no graph file". §16's `tp export` payload carries no `revision`.
finding: The push is gated on `revision`, which §2 defines only as a field of `tp epic export` (a hash of that payload's inputs). In a repository with task files and no graph — a case §1, §3 and §18 rows 2–3 require the dashboard to serve — `tp epic export` exits 3 and there is no `revision`; and with a graph, an unbound task file is not an input of `tp epic export` (§16: unbound files have no place in the graph's contract). Either way a `tp done` on such a file changes no `revision`, so nothing is pushed, yet §18 row 3 requires that close to reach the page.
suggestion: Define the server's push revision over both payloads it sends (the epic export when a graph exists plus `tp export --list`/per-file exports), or give `tp export` and `tp export --list` their own `revision` and push when either changes.

evidence: §2: "pushes it to the page over Server-Sent Events only when its `revision` changed" and "`tp epic export` gains ... `revision` (a hash of the payload's inputs)"; §16 lists `tp export`'s payload with "its own `version: 1`" and no revision; §18 row 3: "an unchanged repository pushes nothing after the first state; a task closed with `tp done` reaches the page | a repo with one task file, two ticks". REFERENCE.md:835 has tp epic status/export exit 3 with no graph file, so that fixture has no epic export to carry a revision.
finding: The push is gated on `tp epic export`'s `revision` alone, but the page also draws `tp export` / `tp export --list` (§12, §13, §16), which carry no `revision`, and the epic export's inputs do not include unbound task files. In a repository with task files and no graph (§3's Specs-first case) there is no epic export at all, and in one with a graph a `tp done` in an unbound file does not change the epic export's inputs. Read literally, §2 never pushes that change, while §18 row 3 requires it to reach the page in exactly a no-graph, one-task-file fixture. Two correct implementations would disagree: one hashes only the epic export's inputs (and so misses task-file changes), the other hashes the whole pushed state.
suggestion: Say what the pushed state's revision covers: the inputs of every payload the server pushes (the epic export when a graph exists, `tp export --list`, and whichever `tp export` the page shows), or give `tp export`/`--list` their own `revision` and push when any of them changes. Also say whether the server pushes every file's `tp export` or the page asks for one with a GET.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md L48-49 ('pushes ... only when its `revision` changed'), L58-59 (revision is added to `tp epic export` only), L363 (`tp export` payload: `version: 1`, no revision), L423 (§18 row 3 fixture has one task file and no graph); round-1 fixed finding on generated_at.
finding: The round-1 repair made the push decision read only `revision`, which §2 defines solely as a field `tp epic export` gains (a hash of that payload's inputs). The page's data is also `tp export`/`tp export --list` (§16), whose payload carries `version: 1` and no revision. A task closed in an unbound task file, or anything at all in a repository with task files and no graph (where there is no epic export to hash), changes no `revision`, so under the repaired text the server never pushes it. That contradicts §18 row 3 (fixture: a repo with one task file; 'a task closed with `tp done` reaches the page') and §3's no-graph mode. The old 'hash the whole result' wording covered both payloads; the repair dropped the task-file half.
suggestion: Say what the push compares across both payloads: e.g. the server pushes when the epic export's `revision` or a revision of the `tp export --list`/`tp export` payloads changed — either give `tp export` its own `revision` (inputs hash, generated_at excluded) or define the push revision as a hash over the inputs of everything the page receives.

evidence: §8: "a gate whose threshold is absent, empty once trimmed, or a placeholder" and Why: "a gate that cannot go green is a decision the operator has not made"; skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:1626: "Green: every member `done` and, when the gate has a `threshold`, a `met` record"; REFERENCE.md:1376: "Every milestone has a gate unit in an epic review"; §7: "gates whose threshold is unwritten or a placeholder".
finding: `gate-threshold-unwritten` counts an absent threshold as unwritten, and its Why says such a gate "cannot go green". In today's contract the threshold is optional and a gate without one goes green as soon as its members are done, with no `--met`. §8 does not say it changes that, so it now warns on (and §7 lists as an operator decision) every working member-only gate. The only way to silence it is to write a threshold, which then makes the gate need a `--met` record it did not need before. It is also undecided whether a milestone with no `gates` entry, which still has a gate unit in an epic review, is a gate "whose threshold is absent". If it is, every such milestone warns.
suggestion: Either limit the rule to a threshold that is present but empty or a placeholder (the gates that really cannot go green, since `gate --met` refuses an empty threshold), or state that this release makes a threshold required and say what happens to existing threshold-less gates. Either way, say whether a milestone with no `gates` entry is in scope.

evidence: §9: 'among the rest, the longest chain of openings is the main lane, milestones that open beside it in the same column are parallel lanes, and milestones nothing on the main chain waits for form a side lane. A milestone's column is its opening depth.' Counterexample: T opens_after [], A [T], B [A], C [B], S [T]. Main lane A-B-C occupies columns 1-3; S (nothing on the main chain waits for it) has depth 1, the same column as A, so the earlier parallel rule takes it and the side lane is empty. §18 row 8 fixture: 'milestones with empty `opens_after`, a main chain, a parallel vertical and a side milestone'.
finding: Under the stated order of precedence the side lane can never hold a milestone, so Tests row 8's 'side milestone' fixture cannot be built. A milestone's column is its opening depth, and the main lane is the longest chain of openings, so the main lane occupies every column from the first non-triggered depth to the deepest; every non-triggered milestone therefore 'opens beside it in the same column' and is a parallel lane before the side-lane rule is reached. A second reading (parallel = a milestone the main chain waits for, side = one it does not, column only positional) does produce side milestones, and the two readings place the same milestone in different lanes.
suggestion: Define parallel by relation, not column alone: a milestone the main chain waits for (directly or through other non-main milestones) is a parallel lane; one nothing on the main chain waits for is the side lane. Keep the column as placement only.

evidence: skills/tp/SKILL.md:838: "`tp epic review --milestone <m>` / `tp epic review --epic <id>` | Emit a graph review round over one slice ... or the one epic"; §11: "`tp epic review <slice> --history` prints the slice's rounds ...; `tp epic review --history --epic <id>` prints one epic's edges and whys per recorded round of every slice whose snapshot holds it" and "exits 3 for a slice with no state directory".
finding: `tp epic review --epic <id>` already names a one-epic slice (it emits that slice's review round). §11 reuses `--epic <id>` with `--history` to mean the epic's history across every slice whose snapshot holds it, while `tp epic review <slice> --history` is a slice's own history. Given an epic that has its own `--epic` slice, `tp epic review --history --epic E1` reads two ways: that slice's rounds (the slice form), or the cross-slice per-epic history. Their output and exit cases differ: §11 has exit 3 for a slice with no state directory, while §11's acceptance has the per-epic form say there is no history.
suggestion: Say which reading `--history --epic <id>` takes and how the epic-slice history is asked for (for example only through the positional `<slice>` key), or give the per-epic form a flag that names no slice.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §17: "tp computes the series in Go and carries each epic's stage times in the export."; skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:1768: `epics` carry `done_at`; REFERENCE.md:1766: `graph` is `.tp/epics.json` as stored; spec §15: "`tp epic export` carries both per bound file."
finding: "carries each epic's stage times in the export" adds a per-epic copy of times the export already carries: `done_at` is on every `epics[]` entry, `claimed.at` is in `graph` as stored, and §15 puts `bound_at` on every bound file. Only the earliest task `started_at` is new. With several hundred epics and an export whose `--compact` is ignored, the duplicate is paid on every agent call. The same sentence says tp "computes the series in Go", leaving open whether a per-day, per-stage series (growing every day of the project) also enters the export beside the times it is computed from.
suggestion: Carry only the stage time the export lacks (the earliest task `started_at`, per epic or per bound file) and state that the per-day series is not part of `tp epic export`; delete the rest of the per-epic copy.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §17 l.393-397: "work epics per stage ... per day ... tp computes the series in Go and carries each epic's stage times in the export"; §2 l.53: "The page computes no figure a tp command reports: every count ... arrives computed"; §2 l.58-61 additions list has no series.
finding: "tp computes the series in Go and carries each epic's stage times in the export" leaves open whether the per-day series itself is in the payload. If only the stage times are carried, the page must bucket them into per-day counts per stage, a figure §2 says it never computes; if the series is carried, the export gains a field §2's list of additions omits.
suggestion: Say the export carries the per-day series (and add it to §2's list), or that the stage times alone are carried and the series is computed in Go for the dashboard payload only.

evidence: §17: '`bound_at` of its bound files specced' ... 'A file bound before this release has no `bound_at`, and the chart shows its binding time as unknown for that epic, never placing it on a guessed day.'
finding: An epic with two bound files, one carrying `bound_at` and one bound before this release without it, has no stated specced time: 'the earliest `bound_at` of its bound files' yields the known file's time, while 'the chart shows its binding time as unknown for that epic' says unknown. One implementation plots the known time, another shows unknown, and the chart and export disagree between them.
suggestion: State whether any bound file lacking `bound_at` makes the epic's specced time unknown (the earliest cannot be known), or whether the earliest recorded `bound_at` is used.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md L394-399 ('the earliest `bound_at` of its bound files specced' and 'A file bound before this release has no `bound_at`, and the chart shows its binding time as unknown for that epic'); §18 row 12 fixture covers only one legacy epic and one with bound_at, not one epic holding both.
finding: The round-1 repair dates specced by 'the earliest `bound_at` of its bound files'. For an epic with two bound files, one bound before this release (no `bound_at`) and one after, the earliest known `bound_at` may be later than the true first binding. One implementation dates specced from the known file (placing the binding on a possibly wrong day, which the same section forbids: 'never placing it on a guessed day'); another shows specced as unknown because one input is unknown. Tests disagree on that epic.
suggestion: State the rule: when any bound file of the epic lacks `bound_at`, its specced time is unknown (or: the earliest known one is used and marked as a lower bound) — and add that mixed epic to §18 row 12's fixture.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §18 row 5: "warns on an empty threshold and on `[threshold]`, `TBD` and the project's own pattern ... | three gates with an empty, a bracketed and a written threshold; a config pattern"; §8 l.180-181: "A project replaces the default with one regular expression"; §8 acceptance: with `^draft:` set, "`[to be agreed]` is not" reported.
finding: Row 5 asks one fixture to show warnings on an empty threshold, `[threshold]`, `TBD` and the project's own pattern, but the fixture has three gates (empty, bracketed, written): no `TBD` gate and no gate matching the project pattern. And under a config pattern §8 says the default is replaced, so `[threshold]` and `TBD` no longer warn alongside the project pattern; the row must be two runs (default, then override), which it does not say.
suggestion: Split the fixture: default pattern over empty, `[threshold]`, `TBD` and written gates; then the override over a `draft:` gate and a bracketed one that must not warn.

evidence: §2: 'pushes it to the page over Server-Sent Events only when its `revision` changed' and '`tp epic export` gains ... `revision` (a hash of the payload's inputs)'; §16 lists `version: 1` but no revision for `tp export`/`--list`, and rejects 'an export key on `tp epic export` (unbound files have no place in the graph's contract)'; §18 row 3: 'a task closed with `tp done` reaches the page' with fixture 'a repo with one task file'.
finding: The push is gated on 'its revision', but `revision` is defined only on `tp epic export`, whose inputs exclude unbound task files (§16), and `tp export` carries no revision. A server that gates on the epic export's revision never pushes a `tp done` in an unbound task file — and in a repository with no graph has no revision at all — which fails Tests row 3; a server that hashes both payloads passes it. The spec does not say which revision the push compares.
suggestion: Say the push compares a revision over everything the page is served (the epic export and every `tp export` payload), or give `tp export`/`--list` their own revision and push when either changes.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §5: "when it is stale, which units changed since its last recorded round and, per unit, what changed in its block (an edge added or removed, a why changed, a field changed)" and "The export's `slices[]` carry the same"; §11: "The last round against the current graph is the stale cause of §5" and "`tp epic review <slice> --history` prints ... the difference from the last round to the current graph".
finding: `tp epic review --status` (and the export's `slices[]`) gains, for every stale slice, the per-unit block change detail (edge added or removed, why changed, field changed). §11 already prints this as "the difference from the last round to the current graph" via `--history`, and calls it the same thing ("The last round against the current graph is the stale cause of §5"). Under `--status --all`/`--milestones` on a several-hundred-epic graph, and in an export with no compact form, every caller now parses per-unit diffs it needs only when it decides to re-review that one slice. The decision `--status` feeds (re-review, grant, leave) needs stale-or-not and which units changed, not the block diff.
suggestion: Keep the changed unit ids in `--status` and `slices[]`; leave the per-unit block change to `tp epic review <slice> --history`, which the page's hover reads.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md L142-145 ('each a count of work epics ... with no graph the phases count task files'); L286 and L361 (unbound files listed with a phase); round-1 fixed finding 12 text vs its recorded fix.
finding: Round-1 finding 12 asked three things; its recorded fix answered the no-graph case and the several-bound-files case but not 'whether unbound files count at all when there is a graph'. §6 still defines the spec-phase counts with a graph as 'a count of work epics', while §12/§16 show unbound task files as first-class rows with a phase. In a repository with a graph and some unbound task files, one implementation leaves them out of the band and another counts them, so the band's phase counts differ from the Specs tab's phase groups.
suggestion: Add one clause to §6: with a graph, unbound task files are (or are not) counted in the spec phases — and if not, say the band's phases then differ from the Specs tab's groups on purpose.

evidence: §7: 'gates whose members are done awaiting `--met`' and 'Deferrable gate members are never listed as waiting, in the operator list, the waiting list or a gate's count'; §6: 'deferrable members left out of both counts'.
finding: 'gates whose members are done awaiting `--met`' does not say whether deferrable members must also be done. A gate whose non-deferrable members are all done but whose deferrable member is open reads 'N of N' in the band (§6) yet may or may not appear as awaiting `--met`; two implementations disagree on whether that row is listed.
suggestion: State that a gate is awaiting `--met` when every non-deferrable member is done (or, if intended, when every member is).

evidence: §9: 'the longest chain of openings is the main lane' and 'The layout is in the export (§2), so the same graph always draws the same way.' Graph: T [], A [T], B [A], X [T], Y [X] — chains A-B and X-Y are both length 2; nothing states which is main.
finding: 'The longest chain of openings is the main lane' has no tie-break when two chains are equally long, yet the section promises 'the same graph always draws the same way' and Tests row 8 asserts each milestone's lane. Two implementations picking different equal-length chains put different milestones in the main and parallel lanes and fail each other's layout tests.
suggestion: State the tie-break (e.g. the chain whose milestones come first in the graph file, or lexicographic by milestone id).

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §16: "each section and paragraph with its anchor" and "it drops each section's body (headings and anchors stay)"; Non-goals: "Feedback on the spec (the anchors are left for it)".
finding: `--compact` drops each section's body but keeps "headings and anchors", which includes one anchor per paragraph. A paragraph anchor whose text is dropped feeds no agent decision this release (the feedback that would use anchors is a non-goal), and it is positional, derivable from the section number and paragraph index.
suggestion: Under `--compact` keep section headings and section anchors only; drop paragraph anchors with the bodies.

evidence: §18 row 5: "warns on an empty threshold and on `[threshold]`, `TBD` and the project's own pattern ... | three gates ...; a config pattern"; §8: "A project replaces the default with one regular expression" and acceptance "a threshold `draft: 80% pass` is reported and `[to be agreed]` is not".
finding: Row 5 asks one fixture with "a config pattern" to warn on `[threshold]`, `TBD` and the project's own pattern. But §8 says a project pattern replaces the default, and §8's own acceptance has `[to be agreed]` not reported once `^draft:` is set. Under the config pattern, `[threshold]` and `TBD` are not placeholders, so the row cannot hold as one run.
suggestion: Split the row: default pattern for `[threshold]`/`TBD`, and the config pattern for the project marker together with a bracketed threshold that is then not reported.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md L201 ('whose `opens_after` entry is `[]`'), L222 ('two milestones have an empty `opens_after`'), L428 (§18 row 8 'milestones with empty `opens_after`'); skills/tp/REFERENCE.md L1375 ('absent, the previous milestone of its track (none for a track's first)').
finding: The lane repair keys the triggered lane on an `opens_after` entry of `[]`, but the acceptance and §18 row 8 say 'an empty `opens_after`'. REFERENCE.md makes a track's first milestone with no entry open after nothing too, so it also has an empty effective opens_after. 'Empty' then reads either as the literal `[]` entry (the repaired rule, keeping the main chain's root out of the triggered lane) or as an effective empty set (putting every track root in the triggered lane and leaving the main lane without a root) — the ambiguity the round-1 finding raised survives in the acceptance wording.
suggestion: Word the acceptance and §18 row 8 as 'an `opens_after` entry of `[]`', and say in §9 that a track's first milestone without an entry is not in the triggered lane.
